chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

Regarding a man who bought food from another man, one load by a known measure, and its owner said to the buyer: Buy from me this other load without measure, for indeed in it is what is in the other one that you bought. He عليه السلام said: It is not valid except by measure.
And he عليه السلام said: Whatever food in which you stipulated a measure, then it is not valid as an unmeasured sale by estimation. This is among what is disapproved in the sale of food.

key_terms.طَعَامًا: food being sold as a commodity
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not valid or proper
key_terms.مُجَازَفَةً: sold by estimation without exact measuring

ai.seo_question: Can food be sold by estimation without measuring it if another measured load was already purchased?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the sale of food commodities when measure has been specified. It states that if food is sold based on a known measure, another similar amount cannot be sold merely by estimation without measuring it. The narration underscores precision and avoidance of uncertainty in food transactions.
